title: Find the Letter
desc: matching a spoken letter name to its printed form (12 cards, 6 uppercase and 6 lowercase)
dir: Listen to your teacher. Point to the letter on your screen.
key: Say: Here are twelve letter cards from the treasure chest. I will say a letter name. Point to the card with that letter.
Say: Point to the letter q. (top row, fourth card)

title: Uppercase Letters
desc: naming all 26 uppercase letters
dir: Say the name of each letter.
key: Show one letter at a time and ask: What is this letter? Mark each letter the student names correctly.
Give no hints and do not say the sound. A name said slowly still counts.

title: Lowercase Letters
desc: naming all 26 lowercase letters
dir: Say the name of each letter.
key: Show one letter at a time and ask: What is this letter? Mark each letter the student names correctly.
b, d, p and q are the ones to watch. Write down which way a mix-up went, such as said d for b.

title: First Sounds
desc: saying the first sound of a pictured word
dir: Listen to your teacher. Say the first sound.
key: Model first: Map. The first sound in map is /m/. Now you try.
Point to the sun. Say: Sun. What is the first sound in sun? (/s/)

title: Rhyme Time
desc: making a rhyme for a given word
dir: Listen to your teacher. Say a word that rhymes.
key: Model first: Log, dog, fog. They rhyme. They sound the same at the end.
Point to the hat. Say: Tell me a word that rhymes with hat. (cat, bat, mat, sat, zat)

title: Slow Parrot
desc: blending syllables and sounds into a word with picture support
dir: Listen to the slow parrot talk. Say the whole word.
key: Say: Pip the parrot talks very slowly. Put the parts together and tell me the word. The pictures can help you. (The pictures are not in the same order as the words.)
Say with a pause between the parts: tur ... tle. (turtle)

title: Pip and the Key
desc: questions about the character, the order of events, and what happens next in a story read aloud
dir: Listen to the story. Then answer out loud.
key: Read the story out loud. Stop after the third sentence, when Pip sees the little box.
Ask at the stopping place: What do you think Pip will do next? (Any guess that fits the story, like try the key in the box or open the box.) Then read the rest.

title: Sea Turtle Facts
desc: making an inference, making a connection, and asking a question about an informational text read aloud
dir: Listen to your teacher read about sea turtles. Then answer out loud.
key: Read the facts out loud. If picture supports are on, the child can look at the picture while listening.

Ask: Why do you think the mother turtle covers her eggs with sand? (A reason that makes sense: to hide them, to keep them safe, or to keep them warm. The text does not say why, so the child has to fig

title: Sound Letters
desc: writing the letter for a beginning sound (m, s, t)
dir: Listen for the sound. Write the letter on your paper and hold it up.
key: Point to the mouse. Say: Mouse starts with /m/. Write the letter that makes the /m/ sound. Hold it up. (m or M)
Point to the star. Say: Star starts with /s/. Write the letter for /s/. (s or S)

title: Label Your Treasure
desc: writing letters to label a drawing
dir: Draw a treasure on your paper. Write letters to tell what it is. Hold it up.
key: Say: Draw your own treasure on your paper. Then write a word or some letters to tell what it is. Hold it up and tell me what you wrote.
Look for: writing that is separate from the drawing (letters or marks that look like letters, not only a picture).

title: Name It
desc: naming objects, actions, and describing words from pictures
dir: Look at each picture. Answer out loud.
key: Picture 1. Say: What is this? (boat, sailboat, or ship)
Picture 2. Say: What is this? (crab)

title: Mystery Chest
desc: asking questions and follow-up questions to find out information
dir: Something is hiding in the chest. Ask your teacher questions to find out what it is.
key: Your secret: a banana is hiding in the chest. Do not tell.
Say: Something is hiding in my treasure chest. Ask me questions to find out what it is. You can ask things like: Is it an animal? What color is it?

title: Would You Rather
desc: sharing an opinion with a reason and details
dir: Pick one. Tell your teacher why.
key: Say: Would you rather sail on the boat or play on the island? Tell me which one and why.
Look for: tells an opinion (picks one).

title: Count the Treasure
desc: counting 10 or more real objects one by one where the teacher can see, then counting groups of 6, 10, and 13 objects one by one on the screen
dir: First count some small things from near you. Then count the pictures on the screen.
key: Start with real things, before the screen. Say: Go and get ten small things you can hold, like spoons, blocks, socks or crayons, and set them on the table where I can see them. Then say: Move each one

Say: Push them back into a pile, add a few more, and count the whole lot again the same way. (Any number past ten. The goal is 10 or more with one number word for each object. If the count breaks down

title: Number Cards
desc: naming the numerals 1 to 10
dir: Say the name of each number.
key: Say: What number is this? Click Next after each one.
Correct means the child says the number name. Write down the ones missed. Watch for 6 and 9 mixed up.

title: More or Fewer
desc: comparing two groups by counting (more, same, fewer)
dir: Look at the pictures. Answer out loud.
key: Top box. Say: Are there more crabs or more fish? How do you know? (More crabs. 5 crabs and 3 fish.)
Middle box. Say: Are there more shells, more stars, or the same number of each? (The same. 4 shells and 4 stars.)

title: Sort the Gems
desc: sorting objects by color and by shape
dir: Look at the gems. Tell which ones go together.
key: Say: These gems got mixed up. Which ones go together? Tell me why. (Sorts by one thing and says what it is. By color: 5 red and 3 blue. By shape: 4 circles and 4 squares.)
Say: Now sort them a different way. (Uses the other way: color if shape came first, shape if color came first.)

title: Picture Chart
desc: reading, copying, and adding to a picture chart with two groups
dir: Look at the chart. Answer out loud. Then make marks on your paper.
key: Say: Some children picked the beach animal they like best, the turtle or the crab. Each face is one child. How many children picked the turtle? (6)
Say: Did more children pick the turtle or the crab? (The turtle. 6 is more than 4.)

title: Name the Shapes
desc: naming, describing, and drawing circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles
dir: Look at the shapes. Answer out loud. Then draw one on your paper.
key: Say: What shape is the red one? (circle)
Say: What shape is the blue one? (square)

title: Where Is It?
desc: position words (on, under, in, between, in front of, up)
dir: Look at the picture. Answer out loud.
key: Say: What is on the table? (the parrot)
Say: What is under the table? (the crab)

title: Flag Line Up
desc: ordering 5 objects by height
dir: Look at the flag poles. Say them in order from shortest to tallest.
key: Say: Which flag pole is the tallest? (green)
Say: Which flag pole is the shortest? (yellow)

title: What Comes Next?
desc: extending repeating patterns and naming the part that repeats
dir: Look at each row. Say what comes next.
key: Top row. Say: Shell, star, shell, star, shell, star, shell. What comes next? (star)
Middle row. Say: Look at this pattern. What comes next? (fish. The pattern is crab, crab, fish, fish.)

title: Uppercase Letters
desc: naming all 26 uppercase letters
dir: Say the name of each letter.
key: Show one letter at a time and ask: What is this letter? Mark each letter the student names correctly.
Give no hints and do not say the sound. A name said slowly still counts.

title: Lowercase Letters
desc: naming all 26 lowercase letters
dir: Say the name of each letter.
key: Show one letter at a time and ask: What is this letter? Mark each letter the student names correctly.
b, d, p and q are the ones to watch. Write down which way a mix-up went, such as said d for b.

title: Letter Sounds
desc: saying the most common sound for all 26 letters
dir: Say the sound each letter makes.
key: Show one letter at a time and ask: What sound does this letter make? Mark each correct sound.
For a, e, i, o and u the short sound is what is expected. The long sound is also correct.

title: Book Parts
desc: print concepts (finding the title, where to start, which way to read, and the first and last word of a line)
dir: Look at the page. Point or answer out loud.
text: The Treasure Map I see a big map We can dig here
key: Say: This is a page from a book. Point to the title. (the big words in the banner at the top: The Treasure Map. If the student cannot point on the screen, they can tell you where it is.)
Ask: Where do I start reading? Point to it. (the first word of the top line, on the left: I)

title: Sound Games
desc: rhyming, clapping syllables, blending sounds, and saying the sounds in spoken words
dir: Listen to your teacher. Answer out loud.
key: Ask: Do cat and hat rhyme? (yes)
Ask: Tell me a word that rhymes with bug. (rug, hug, mug, any rhyme, silly words count)

title: Read the Words
desc: reading high-frequency words and short vowel words
dir: Read each word out loud.
text: the I see like my can cat sun pig
key: High-frequency words by sight: the, I, see, like, my, can
Sounds out or reads: cat, sun, pig

title: Little Book
desc: reading a short emergent-reader book
dir: Point to each word and read it out loud.
text: I see a cat. I see the cat. I like the cat. The cat can sit. The cat can nap. The cat can run. I pat the cat. I like my cat.
key: Count the words the student reads correctly, out of 32, and enter the number in the box. A word the student fixes without help counts. Write down the words that were missed.
Points or tracks left to right and top to bottom

title: Listen to the Cat Lines
desc: asking and answering key detail questions about story lines read aloud to the student
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the lines. Then answer out loud.
text: The cat sat on my mat. I can see a big bug. The cat can get the bug.
key: Read the three cat lines on the screen out loud to the student two times. Point under each word as you read. The student does not read them. Ask: What did the cat sit on? (my mat)
Ask: What can the cat get? (the bug)

title: Ben the Bear
desc: answering key detail questions about a story read aloud
dir: Put your eyes on your teacher and listen. Then answer out loud.
text: Listening time. Your teacher will read you a story about a bear and his hat.
key: Read the bear story aloud. Ask: Who is the story about? (Ben the bear)
Ask: What did Ben lose? (his red hat)

title: Listen and Learn
desc: asking and answering key detail questions about an informational text read aloud to the student
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the lines. Then answer out loud.
text: A duck can swim. A duck has big feet. A duck can get a bug.
key: Read the three lines on the screen out loud to the student two times. Point under each word as you read. The student does not read them. Ask: What can a duck do? (swim, or get a bug. Line 1 or line 3.
Ask: What does a duck have? (big feet. Line 2.)

title: Talk About It
desc: describing a favorite place with details
dir: Tell your teacher out loud. Use lots of details.
text: Tell me about your favorite place to play.
key: Describes the place
Adds more detail when you ask: What do you do there? What does it look like?

title: Word Fun
desc: spoken grammar items (plural nouns, question words, complete sentences)
dir: Listen to your teacher. Say your answer out loud.
key: Say: One dog, two ____. (dogs)
Say: One wish, two ____. (wishes)

title: Find Out
desc: answering questions from a picture chart and from experience
dir: Look at the chart. Answer out loud.
qs: Look at the chart. What do we get from a hen?
Look at the chart. What do we get from a bee?
key: Eggs. Uses the chart to answer
Honey. Uses the chart to answer

title: Animal Facts
desc: an informative draw-and-write piece
dir: Draw and write on your paper. Hold it up when you finish.
text: Draw an animal you know. Write its name. Then write or tell one thing about it.
key: Names what the picture and writing are about (W.K.2)
Gives at least one piece of information about it (W.K.2)

title: What I Like
desc: an opinion draw-and-write piece
dir: Draw and write on your paper. Hold it up when you finish.
text: sunny day rainy day Which do you like more: sunny days or rainy days? Draw it. Then write or tell which one you like best.
key: Tells the topic: sunny days or rainy days (W.K.1)
States an opinion or preference, such as: I like rainy days (W.K.1)

title: My Story
desc: a narrative draw-and-write piece
dir: Draw and write on your paper. Hold it up when you finish.
text: Think of something fun you did. Draw it. Then write or tell what happened first and what happened next. Tell how you felt. First Next I felt
key: Tells about one thing that happened, or a few things that go together (W.K.3)
Tells the events in the order they happened (W.K.3)

title: Where Is It?
desc: using in, on, and under to tell where something is
dir: Look at each picture. Say your answer out loud.
key: Ask: Look at picture 1. Where is the parrot? (in the box. in or inside counts)
Ask: Look at picture 2. Where is the parrot? (on the table. on or on top counts)

title: Count Out Loud
desc: counting to 100 by ones and by tens
dir: Count out loud for your teacher.
text: Count out loud as high as you can. Then count by tens.
key: Counts by ones. Stop at 100. Write the highest number reached before an error.
Counts by tens to 100: 10, 20, 30 ... 100

title: How Many
desc: counting objects, telling one more, and counting on from a given number
dir: Point to each dot and count out loud.
qs: How many dots? Count them.
If I add one more dot, how many will there be?
key: 8, touching or pointing to each dot once
9, without recounting

title: Count On
desc: counting on from a given number and telling the number that is one more
dir: Listen to your teacher. Count out loud.
text: Count with your teacher.
key: Say: Start at 4 and keep counting up. Stop at 9. (5, 6, 7, 8, 9. The student does not go back to 1.)
Say: Start at 12 and count up to 16. (13 to 16)

title: More or Less
desc: comparing two groups of objects (more and fewer)
dir: Look at the dots. Answer out loud.
qs: Which group has more dots?
Which group has fewer dots?
key: Group B (9)
Group A (6)

title: Add and Take Away
desc: addition and subtraction word problems and facts within 10
dir: Listen to your teacher read each one. Use your fingers or draw. Then say the answer.
qs: 3 frogs sit on a log. 2 more frogs hop on. How many frogs now?
6 birds are in a tree. 2 fly away. How many birds are left?
key: 5 frogs
4 birds

title: Break Apart
desc: breaking 5 and 8 into pairs of numbers
dir: Use your fingers or draw on your paper. Then tell your teacher.
qs: Show one way to make 5.
Show a different way to make 5.
key: First way to make 5: 0 + 5, 1 + 4, or 2 + 3, shown with fingers, a drawing, or numbers
Second way to make 5 that is different from the first

title: Split It
desc: breaking a number up to 10 into two parts in more than one way and recording each way
dir: Look at the picture. Draw or write on your paper. Hold it up when you finish.
text: Here are 7.
key: Say: Show me one way to split these 7 into two groups. Draw it or write it with numbers, such as 3 + 4 = 7. (a drawing with two groups, or an equation, that makes 7)
Say: Now show me a different way. (a second pair of parts that make 7. The same two numbers in the other order do not count as different.)

title: Ten and Some More
desc: showing a number from 11 to 19 as a ten and some more and recording it
dir: Look at the picture. Draw or write on your paper. Hold it up when you finish.
text: Look at the full ten frame and the extra ones.
key: Say: Show 14 as a ten and some more. Draw it or write it with numbers, such as 14 = 10 + 4. (a drawing of a ten and 4 more, or the equation)
Ask: How many ones are left after the ten? (4)

title: Teen Numbers
desc: teen numbers as ten ones and some more ones
dir: Look at the dots. Answer out loud.
qs: How many dots in all?
This number is ten and how many more?
key: 4 (14 is ten and 4 more)

title: Longer or Shorter
desc: comparing the lengths of two objects
dir: Look at the bars. Answer out loud.
qs: Which bar is longer?
Which bar is shorter?
key: A
B

title: Sort and Count
desc: sorting shapes, counting each group, and comparing the counts
dir: Look at the shapes. Count out loud.
qs: How many circles? How many squares? How many triangles?
Which shape has the most?
key: 4 circles, 2 squares, 3 triangles
Circles (4)

title: Heavy or Light
desc: comparing two objects by weight to say which is heavier and which is lighter
dir: Look at the scales. Answer out loud.
text: A B
key: Ask: Look at scale A. Which one is heavier? (the chest. It is on the side that goes down.)
Ask: Which one is lighter? (the coin)

title: Where Is It
desc: naming shapes and telling where they are (above, below, beside)
dir: Look at the shapes. Answer out loud.
qs: Name each shape.
Which shape is above the square?
key: Circle, square, triangle, rectangle
Circle

title: Flat or Solid
desc: telling flat shapes from solid shapes
dir: Answer out loud.
qs: Is a ball flat or solid?
Is a circle drawn on paper flat or solid?
key: Solid
Flat

title: What Living Things Need
desc: telling what plants and animals need to stay alive
dir: Look at each row. Answer out loud.
text: A plant and a dog both live on the island. Living things need certain things to stay alive.
qs: A plant needs two of these to grow. Which two? Sunlight, water, or a hat?
A dog needs two of these. Which two? Food, water, or a book?
key: sunlight and water. A hat is not something a plant needs.
food and water. A book is not something a dog needs.

title: Weather on the Island
desc: describing a weather pattern from a week of observations
dir: Look at the week of weather. Answer out loud.
text: Here is one week of weather on the island. Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri
qs: How many sunny days were there?
How many rainy days were there?

title: Weather on the Island
desc: telling how a living thing changes its surroundings to get what it needs
dir: Answer out loud.
text: A bird on the island wants a safe place for its eggs.
qs: The bird gathers twigs and grass and builds a nest in the tree. Did the bird change the tree, or did the tree change the bird?
Tell me one way you change your room to get what you need.
key: The bird changed the tree. It added a nest that was not there before.
Any sensible answer about changing a space on purpose: moving a chair to reach a shelf, opening a window when it is hot, turning on a lamp to see.

title: Homes, Forecasts and the Land
desc: matching animals to the places that give them what they need
dir: Match each animal to the place it lives. Answer out loud.
text: Each animal lives in one place. It gets what it needs. The places are: a cave, a tree, the water.
qs: Where does the fish live?
Where does the bird live?
key: the water
a tree

title: Homes, Forecasts and the Land
desc: telling what a weather forecast is for
dir: Answer out loud.
text: Every morning the crew listens to the weather report before they go out.
qs: Why do they listen to the weather report? To know if a big storm is coming, or to hear a song?
What could the crew do if the report said a big storm was coming?
key: to know if a big storm is coming.
Any sensible answer: stay in, wait a day, pack a warm coat, tie the sled down.

title: Homes, Forecasts and the Land
desc: telling one way people can take better care of the land and water
dir: Answer out loud.
text: Two children finish a snack on the beach.
qs: One child puts the wrapper in the trash can. One child drops it on the sand. Which choice is better for the island?
Tell me one more way to take care of the land or the water.
key: putting the wrapper in the trash can
Any sensible answer: pick up litter, turn off the tap, do not pour things in the water, plant something, reuse a bag.

title: Pushes and Pulls
desc: telling a push from a pull, and comparing a hard push with a gentle one
dir: Answer out loud. Do not say push or pull for the student.
text: A push moves something away from you. A pull brings it toward you.
qs: You drag a sled behind you by its rope. Is that a push or a pull?
You kick a ball away from you. Is that a push or a pull?
key: a pull
a push

title: Pushes and Pulls
desc: deciding whether a change made a thing move faster or in a new direction
dir: Answer out loud.
text: The crew rolls the same ball down two ramps and marks where it stops. Ramp How far the ball rolled a steep ramp 8 steps a flat ramp 3 steps
qs: Which ramp sent the ball farther?
The ball is rolling to the right. You give it a push from the right side. Which way does it go now?
key: the steep ramp, 8 steps
to the left. The push changes the direction it was going.

title: Sun and Shade
desc: telling what sunlight does to the ground
dir: Answer out loud. If you can, feel a sunny spot and a shady spot together first.
text: Two trays of sand sit out on the island all morning. One is in the sun. One is under a palm tree.
qs: What makes the ground warm, the sun or the moon?
Which tray of sand is warmer, the one in the sun or the one in the shade?
key: the sun
the one in the sun

title: Sun and Shade
desc: designing and drawing something that keeps a spot cooler
dir: Draw your answer on your paper and hold it up.
text: A bench is on the island. It is too hot. You cannot sit on it. Draw something over the bench to make shade, like an umbrella, a roof, or a tree.
qs: Draw your shade cover over the bench.
Tell me how your cover keeps the bench cooler.
key: Any cover drawn ABOVE the bench. The three examples are in the direction, so copying one still counts. A wall drawn beside the bench is partial: ask where the sun is coming from.
Something like: it blocks the sun, the sun cannot reach the bench, it makes a shadow.

title: Solving a Problem
desc: naming a problem people want to fix and asking about it
dir: Listen, then answer out loud.
qs: What is the problem? The crayons roll off the table, or the crayons are red?
Ask me one question that would help you fix it.
key: The crayons roll off the table.
Any real question: how far do they roll, how many are there, is the table flat, can we move the table. A statement is not a question, so ask once more.

title: Solving a Problem
desc: drawing something whose shape would solve the problem
dir: Draw your answer on your paper and hold it up.
text: Draw something that would keep the crayons on the table, like a box, a tray, or a wall along the edge.
qs: Draw your fix.
Tell me what you drew and how its shape stops the rolling.
key: Any tool that would stop a roll: a box, a cup, a tray, a rim or wall along the edge, a strip of tape. The three examples are in the direction, so copying one earns credit.
Naming it is what shows intent. Something like: the wall stops them, the box holds them in.

title: Solving a Problem
desc: comparing test results from two fixes for the same problem
dir: Look at the chart. Answer out loud.
text: The crew tried two fixes and counted how many crayons fell each time. Fix Crayons that fell a tray with a rim 0 a strip of tape 4
qs: Which fix worked better?
How do you know?
key: the tray with a rim
Because 0 crayons fell with the tray and 4 fell with the tape. The reason has to come from the chart, not from liking trays.

title: Rules and Doing Right
desc: following rules, knowing what happens when they are broken, and naming an honest choice
dir: Listen, then answer out loud.
qs: What did Mia choose to do? Tell the truth, or hide and say nothing?
One rule on the ship is take turns. What might happen if you do not take turns?
key: She told the truth.
A friend feels sad and may not want to play. Any real consequence counts.

title: Maps and Places
desc: telling land from water on a map, using position words, and naming places in a neighborhood
dir: Look at the map. Answer out loud.
text: Here is a map of the island. the cabin the tree
qs: On a map, which part is water and which part is land?
The cabin is on the left. The tree is on the right. Which one is on the left?
key: The blue part is water and the green or brown part is land.
the cabin

title: Left and Right
desc: telling where things are with left and right, near and far, and in front and behind
dir: Look at each picture. Point or answer out loud.
text: A B C
key: Ask: Look at picture A. Point to the one on the left. (the crab)
Ask: Point to the one on the right. (the parrot)

title: Our Flag and Long Ago
desc: recognizing the flag as a symbol of the country
dir: Answer out loud.
qs: What is this?
Where have you seen one?
key: a flag. Accept the flag of our country or the American flag.
Any real place: a school, a post office, a park, outside a building, at a game.

title: Our Flag and Long Ago
desc: telling what a holiday honors and how life long ago was different from life today
dir: Answer out loud.
text: Long ago there were no cars.
qs: How did people travel from place to place long ago, with a horse and wagon or with a car?
How do you travel today?
key: a horse and wagon
Any real answer: a car, a bus, a plane, walking, a bike. Naming today's way is the then-and-now half of this standard.

title: Sound Game
desc: blending and segmenting sounds in spoken words
dir: Listen to your teacher. Say the sounds and words out loud.
key: Blend: /s/ /t/ /o/ /p/ (stop)
Blend: /f/ /l/ /a/ /g/ (flag)

title: Word Flip
desc: reading words with digraphs, final e, vowel teams, endings, and two syllables
dir: Read each word out loud. The last two are silly words. Just sound them out.
key: Read each word. thap and bame are silly words: listen for th and the silent e.
Watch for: digraphs (ship, chin), final e (cake, bike), vowel teams (rain, seed), ending -ed (jumped), two syllables (sunset, rabbit), tricky word (said).

title: Read the Story
desc: a 73-word grade-level story read aloud
dir: Read the story out loud. Use your best reading voice.
text: Fox had a big red hat. He wore it every sunny day. It was his best hat. One windy morning, Fox went for a walk. He walked by the pond. Whoosh! The wind took his
key: 73 words. Mark errors and self-corrections on the large-print passage in the record sheet.
Note pace, expression, and whether the student rereads to fix mistakes.

title: Read It Again
desc: reading the same on-level text orally a second time with accuracy, rate, and expression
dir: Read the same text one more time. Make it smoother and more expressive.
text: Fox had a big red hat. He wore it every sunny day. It was his best hat. One windy morning, Fox went for a walk. He walked by the pond. Whoosh! The wind took his
key: Second reading of the same text. Count the words read correctly again and compare with the first reading. More words read correctly, fewer stops and rereads, and smoother phrasing show growth on succe
After the second reading ask: “What was the story about? What happened first?” (a summary or answer that matches the text on the screen)

title: Story Questions
desc: key detail questions about a story
dir: Listen to each question. Answer out loud.
qs: What did the wind do to Fox’s hat?
What did Fox do to try to get his hat?
key: Blew it up into a tall tree (RL.1.1)
Jumped and jumped (RL.1.1)

title: Sentence Detective
desc: finding the first word and end mark of a sentence
dir: Look at the story again. Answer out loud.
text: Fox had a big red hat. He wore it every sunny day. It was his best hat. One windy morning, Fox went for a walk. He walked by the pond. Whoosh! The wind took his
qs: Find the first word of any sentence. Read that word to me. How do you know a sentence starts there?
Find the end of any sentence. What is the mark at the end called?
key: Reads the first word of a sentence and says it starts with a capital letter (RF.1.1)
Finds a period, exclamation mark, or question mark and names it (RF.1.1)

title: Fix It Fast
desc: spoken grammar items (verb tense, pronouns, joining sentences, questions)
dir: Listen to your teacher read each one. Say your answer out loud.
qs: Today I walk. Yesterday I ____.
Today I jump. Tomorrow I ____ jump.
key: walked
will

title: Which Word Fits?
desc: using indefinite pronouns such as everyone, anyone, someone, something, and nothing
dir: Listen to the sentence. Say the word that fits.
qs: Which word fits? ___ in our class likes to sing. (Everyone / Nothing)
Which word fits? I looked in the box, but there was ___ in it. (anyone / nothing)
key: Everyone. (Say the whole sentence with the word. Other correct pronouns that make sense also count.)
nothing. (Say the whole sentence with the word. Other correct pronouns that make sense also count.)

title: Commands and Big Feelings
desc: producing imperative (command) and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts
dir: Listen. Say your answer out loud in a full sentence.
qs: Tell me to open the door. Say it as a command.
You see a rainbow! Say one sentence that shows a big feeling.
key: A command such as “Open the door.” or “Please open the door.”
An exclamation such as “What a big rainbow!” or “Look how pretty it is!”

title: Tell Me About It
desc: describing a favorite place with details
dir: Talk for about one minute. Speak clearly.
text: Tell me about your favorite place. What do you see there? What do you do there? How do you feel there?
key: Names the place and gives 2 or more details about what is there (SL.1.4)
Names 2 or more people, things, or events at the place and tells something about one of them (SL.1.4)

title: Person, Place, Thing, Event
desc: describing a person, a place, a thing, and an event with relevant details, and saying ideas and feelings clearly
dir: Listen to your teacher. Tell about each one. Use lots of details.
text: Tell about a person, a place, a thing, and something that happened.
key: Say: “Tell me about someone in your family or a friend.” (gives at least 2 relevant details about the person, such as who they are, what they look like, or what they do)
Say: “Tell me about a place you like to go.” (gives at least 2 relevant details about the place, such as what is there or what you do there)

title: Frog Facts
desc: key detail questions about an informational text
dir: Listen while your teacher reads about frogs. Then answer out loud.
text: Frogs live near ponds. They like the wet grass. A frog starts as an egg. The egg is in the water. The egg hatches. Out comes a tadpole. A tadpole has a tail. It
qs: What hatches out of a frog egg?
What does a frog use to catch bugs?
key: A tadpole (RI.1.1)
Its long, sticky tongue (RI.1.1)

title: Listen Up
desc: asking and answering questions after listening to a text read aloud
dir: Listen carefully. Your teacher will read about bees. Then answer out loud.
key: What do bees make from nectar? (honey) (SL.1.2)
How does a bee show other bees where the flowers are? (wiggle dance) (SL.1.2)

title: Two-Step Directions
desc: giving, restating, and following simple two-step directions
dir: Listen to your teacher. Do what you hear, say it back, and give a direction of your own.
text: Listen carefully. Do what your teacher says. You need a pencil and paper.
key: Say once, without repeating: “Touch your nose, then clap two times.” (does both steps, in the right order)
Say once, without repeating: “Stand up, then turn around.” (does both steps, in the right order)

title: Opinion Writing
desc: an opinion writing piece
dir: Write on your paper. When you finish, hold it up and tell your teacher what you wrote.
text: Was Duck a good friend to Fox? Write what you think and tell why. Use the story. Write 2 or 3 sentences. Look back at the story Fox had a big red hat. He wore i
key: Names the story or topic (W.1.1)
States an opinion (W.1.1)

title: Facts Writing
desc: an informative writing piece
dir: Write on your paper. When you finish, hold it up and tell your teacher what you wrote.
text: Write about frogs. Tell 2 facts you learned from Frog Facts. Write 2 or 3 sentences. Look back at Frog Facts Frogs live near ponds. They like the wet grass. A f
key: Names the topic (W.1.2)
Gives at least 2 facts (W.1.2)

title: Story Writing
desc: a narrative writing piece
dir: Write on your paper. When you finish, hold it up and tell your teacher what you wrote.
text: Write about a time something blew away or got lost. Tell what happened first, next, and last. First Next Last
key: Tells 2 or more events in order (W.1.3)
Includes some details about what happened (W.1.3)

title: Remember and Tell
desc: recalling information from experiences to answer a question
dir: Think about what happened to you. Tell your teacher your answer out loud. You can draw it, too.
qs: Think about getting ready for bed. Tell me two things you do.
Think about breakfast. What did you eat today or yesterday? Tell me about it.
key: Gives two real things the student does at bedtime. Any true answer counts.
Names a real food or meal from experience. (They may draw first, then tell. Write down what they say if you want a record.)

title: Count On
desc: counting on and back to add and subtract
dir: Answer out loud.
qs: Start at 7. Count on 3. Where do you land? What adding sentence is that?
Start at 12. Count back 2. What taking away sentence is that?

title: Count to 120
desc: counting, reading, and writing numbers to 120
dir: Count and read out loud. Write your numbers on your paper and hold it up.
qs: Count out loud from 96 to 112.
Read these numbers out loud: 58, 104, 119.
key: Fifty-eight, one hundred four, one hundred nineteen (1.NBT.A.1)

title: Tens and Ones
desc: tens and ones in two-digit numbers
dir: Look at the blocks. Answer out loud.
qs: What number is this? How many tens and ones?
What does the 1 in 15 mean?
key: 46. 4 tens and 6 ones (1.NBT.B.2)
1 ten, or 10 (1.NBT.B.2)

title: Word Problems
desc: addition and subtraction word problems within 20
dir: Listen to each problem. You can draw on your paper. Hold it up when you finish.
qs: Eli has 9 shells. He finds some more. Now he has 15. How many did he find? Write a number sentence with a box for the number you don’t know.
Ana has 12 stickers. Ben has 8. How many more stickers does Ana have?

title: Number Tricks
desc: using properties of addition as strategies
dir: Answer out loud. Tell how you know.
qs: 8 + 3 = 11. So what is 3 + 8?
Add 4 + 7 + 6. Which two numbers would you add first? Why?
key: 11, knows without counting (1.OA.B.3)
17. Adds 4 + 6 to make 10, then 10 + 7 (1.OA.B.3)

title: What Was at the Start?
desc: solving addition and subtraction word problems within 20 where the start is unknown, using a symbol for the unknown number
dir: Listen to the story problem. You can draw. Write a number sentence with a box for the number you do not know. Say your answer.
qs: Some ducks were in the pond. Then 5 more ducks came. Now there are 12 ducks. How many ducks were in the pond at the start? Write a number sentence with a box for the missing number.
Mia had some stickers. She gave 4 away. Now she has 9 left. How many stickers did Mia have at the start? Write a number sentence with a box.
key: 13 stickers. □ - 4 = 9

title: Big Adding
desc: adding within 100
dir: Solve each one. Say 1 and 2 out loud. Show your work for 3 on your paper and hold it up.
key: 66, adds tens to tens (1.NBT.C.4)

title: Take Away Tens
desc: subtracting multiples of 10
dir: Solve each one. Tell how you know.
qs: 90 - 50. Show how you know.
key: 40, uses tens (9 tens take away 5 tens) and explains (1.NBT.C.6)

title: Pet Graph
desc: finishing and reading a bar graph with three categories
dir: Tell your teacher how many squares to color for fish. Then answer out loud.
text: 3 kids like fish. Finish the graph.
qs: How many kids are on the graph in all?
How many more kids like dogs than cats?
key: Fish bar filled to 3. Click the squares as the student tells you.
6 + 4 + 3 = 13 kids in all

title: Make a Graph
desc: organizing and representing data with up to three categories, and answering questions about the total and about how many more or less
dir: Look at the list. Make a tally chart or a picture graph on your paper. Then answer out loud.
text: Ten kids told us their favorite fruits. apple banana apple grape apple banana apple grape banana apple
key: A chart or graph with apple 5, banana 3, grape 2. Each item is counted once. Tally marks, pictures, or squares all work. Labels are on each group.
10 (the total of all three groups)

title: Measure It
desc: measuring length with same-size units
dir: Look at the pictures. Answer out loud.
qs: How many paper clips long is the pencil?
Is the crayon measured the right way? Why or why not?
key: 5 paper clips (1.MD.A.2)
No. The clips have gaps between them (1.MD.A.2)

title: Clock Time
desc: telling time to the hour and half hour
dir: Write the times for A and B on your paper and hold it up.
qs: Write the time on Clock A.
Write the time on Clock B.

title: Fair Shares
desc: halves and fourths of circles and rectangles
dir: Look at the shapes. Answer out loud. Draw the last one on your paper.
qs: What do we call the yellow part of the circle?
Which rectangle shows halves? How do you know?
key: A fourth, a quarter, or one of four equal parts (1.G.A.3)
B. The parts are the same size (1.G.A.3)

title: Copy an Animal Part
desc: naming the job an animal body part does, then designing a tool that copies it to solve a human problem
dir: Look at the pictures. Answer the first two out loud. Draw the third on your paper and hold it up.
text: A duck walks over soft wet mud. It walks all day. It does not sink. Its feet are wide and flat. The crew cross the beach. They carry a heavy load. They sink int
qs: How do wide, flat feet help a duck stay on top of soft mud?
Draw a sand shoe for the crew that copies the duck's wide, flat foot.
key: The weight is spread out over a bigger space, so the foot presses down less in any one spot. Any answer about spreading the weight or being wide counts.
Any shoe drawn wider and flatter than a boot: a board, a paddle shape, a flat oval strapped on. A shoe drawn the same size as a boot is partial, so ask what the duck's foot is like.

title: Parents and Young
desc: finding a pattern in what a parent animal does and what the young do in answer, and saying how it helps the young
dir: Listen while your teacher reads. Then answer out loud.
qs: What do the young do every single time the parent lands on the nest?
What do the young do when they hear the one short call?
key: They open their beaks wide. The point is that it happens every time, which is what makes it a pattern.
They settle down low in the nest and stay there until the soft call.

title: Parents and Young
desc: making observations that young plants and animals are like their parents but not exactly like them
dir: Look at the two pairs. Answer out loud.
text: A young palm and a grown palm. A young parrot and a grown parrot.
qs: Name one way the young palm is like the grown palm.
Name one way the young palm is not exactly like the grown palm.
key: Both have a green stem and leaves, both are plants, both grow out of the ground. Any likeness the picture shows counts.
The young one is much shorter, it has fewer leaves, it has no trunk yet. Any difference the picture shows counts.

title: Sun, Moon and Stars
desc: finding a pattern in a log of sky observations and using it to predict what comes next
dir: Look at the log. Answer out loud.
text: The crew wrote down the sky for four days. Day Where the sun came up Where the sun went down Monday over the east point behind the west rocks Tuesday over the e
qs: Where did the sun come up on every one of the four days?
Where did the sun go down on every one of the four days?
key: over the east point
behind the west rocks

title: Sun, Moon and Stars
desc: relating the number of hours of daylight to the time of year from observations made across a year
dir: Look at the chart. Answer out loud.
text: The crew counted the hours of daylight four times in one year. Time of year Hours of daylight summer 14 fall 12 winter 10 spring 12
qs: Which time of year had the most hours of daylight?
Which time of year had the fewest?
key: summer, 14 hours
winter, 10 hours

title: Sound and Shaking
desc: planning an investigation showing that a shaking material makes sound and that a sound can make a material shake
dir: If you have a rubber band and a box, try the first part first. Either way, answer out loud.
text: Stretch a rubber band across an open box. Pluck it once and watch it closely while you listen. Now put a few grains of dry sand on a piece of cloth pulled tight
qs: While you hear the sound, what is the rubber band doing?
Now pinch the band so it cannot move. What happens to the sound, and why?
key: Shaking back and forth very fast. Buzzing, wobbling, vibrating, blurry, all count.
The sound stops. Nothing is shaking any more, and no shaking means no sound.

title: Seeing in the Dark
desc: accounting for why an object in darkness can be seen only when light shines on it
dir: Answer out loud.
text: The hold under the deck has no window. When the hatch is shut, no light gets in at all.
qs: The chest is sitting in the hold with the hatch shut. Can you see it? Say why or why not.
What do you need to bring down there so you can see the chest?
key: No. There is no light in the hold, and you cannot see a thing unless light shines on it and comes back to your eyes.
A light: a lantern or a flashlight. Accept opening the hatch to let light in.

title: Seeing in the Dark
desc: using test results to tell what happens when different materials are put in the path of a beam of light
dir: Look at the test results. Answer out loud.
text: The crew shone one flashlight beam at four things and wrote down what the beam did. What was put in the beam What the beam did a clear glass bottle went straigh
qs: Which thing let almost all the light go straight through?
Which thing stopped the light and made a dark shadow?
key: the clear glass bottle
the wooden board

title: A Message Far Away
desc: designing a device that uses light or sound to send a message over a distance too far to shout
dir: Draw your answer on your paper. Then answer out loud.
text: The lookout stands up high. The hill top is where he stands. The rest of the crew is below. They are on the beach. It is far down. They are much too far apart.
qs: Draw a device the lookout could use to tell the beach crew that the boat is back. It has to use light or sound.
Tell me what you drew and whether it uses light or sound.
key: Any device that makes light or sound carry: a lantern held up, a mirror catching the sun, a horn, a bell, a drum, a whistle. A written sign does not count, because writing cannot be read from that far
Names it and says which one it uses. Light for a lantern or a mirror, sound for a horn or a bell.

title: Fix the Blowing Map
desc: naming a problem people want to change, asking a question about it, and saying what to observe first
dir: Listen while your teacher reads. Then answer out loud.
qs: What is the problem the crew wants to change?
Ask me one question that would help you fix it.
key: The wind keeps lifting a corner of the map and folding it over.
Any real question: which corner lifts, how strong is the wind, how big is the map, is the table flat, is there anything heavy nearby. A statement is not a question, so ask once more.

title: Fix the Blowing Map
desc: making a simple drawing of a fix and explaining how the shape of the object makes it work
dir: Draw your answer on your paper and hold it up. Then answer out loud.
text: Draw something that holds the map flat on the table while the wind blows.
qs: Draw your fix on the map and the table.
Point to the part that does the holding and tell me its shape.
key: Any holder that would really hold: a heavy stone on each corner, a rim or frame round the edge, clips, a strip of wood along the top, a clear sheet weighted down.
Names a shape: round and heavy, a long bar, a hook that grips over the edge, a frame all the way round.

title: Which Fix Worked
desc: comparing the data from tests of two objects built to solve the same problem
dir: Look at the chart. Answer out loud.
text: The crew built two map holders and tested each one in ten gusts of wind. They counted how many times a corner lifted. Holder Times a corner lifted, out of 10 fo
qs: Which holder worked better in the test?
How do you know, using the numbers in the chart?
key: the four smooth stones
A corner lifted only 1 time out of 10 with the stones and 6 times out of 10 with the tape, so the stones held better. The numbers have to be in the answer.

title: Rights and Jobs
desc: telling a right from a responsibility and naming a responsibility that goes with a right
dir: Listen while your teacher reads. Then answer out loud.
qs: Name one right from the first list.
Name one responsibility from the second list.
key: A turn with the spyglass, a safe place to sleep, or saying what you think at the meeting.
Putting tools back, helping carry the water, or listening while someone else talks.

title: Where Things Are
desc: giving an exact grid location, describing a relative location, telling a physical feature from a built one, naming the ocean a place sits in, and knowing how many continents and oceans the world has
dir: Look at the map grid. Answer out loud.
text: A map of the island, drawn on a grid. 1 2 3 A B C palm tree the Pacific Ocean the cabin the supply chest the hill The top of this map is north. The bottom is so
qs: Find the cabin. Give its exact spot on the grid, the letter and the number.
Where is the palm tree compared to the cabin? Use north, south, east or west.
key: B2. Both parts are needed. B alone or 2 alone is partial. (HSS-1.2)
North of the cabin and west of it. Both directions are needed for a full answer, and north west counts. (HSS-1.2)

title: Where Things Are
desc: naming built features of a familiar place and recognizing that people in one place come from many different places
dir: Answer out loud about your own neighborhood.
text: Think about the street you live on and the streets near it.
qs: Name two things in your neighborhood that people built.
People who live on the same street often came from many different places. Name one thing a family might bring with them from the place they used to live.
key: Any two built things: houses, a store, a school, a road, a sidewalk, a park bench, a fire station, a bus stop. A tree or a hill does not count here.
Any real answer: the language they speak at home, the food they cook, a song, a game, the way they say hello.

title: Symbols, Then and Now
desc: telling what a national symbol stands for and naming a tradition that shows people belong to the same country
dir: Look at the pictures. Answer out loud.
text: A flag stands for a country. The United States flag has 50 stars. It has 13 stripes. The bald eagle stands for the country. That country is the United States.
qs: How many stars are on the flag of the United States, and what does each one stand for?
What does a symbol do? Does it stand for something bigger, or is it only a picture?
key: 50 stars, one for each state.
It stands for something bigger. The flag is cloth, but it stands for the whole country.

title: Symbols, Then and Now
desc: comparing everyday life long ago with life today and telling what changed from what stayed the same
dir: Look at the chart. Answer out loud.
text: Finding your way across the water. Long ago Today finding the way the stars and a compass a screen that shows the map sending word home a letter that rode on a
qs: Long ago, how did a sailor find the way across the water?
How does someone find the way across the water today?
key: By the stars and a compass.
With a screen that shows the map. Accept a phone, a map on a screen, or a satellite.

title: Word Flip
desc: reading words with long and short vowels, vowel teams, a prefix, a suffix, and irregular spellings
dir: Read each word out loud. The last two are silly words. Just sound them out.
key: Read each word. snoat and plaim are silly words: listen for the oa and ai vowel team sounds.
Watch for: long vs short vowel (hope, tap), vowel teams (boat, cloud, chew, rainbow), prefix and suffix (unlock, helpful), irregular words (laugh, busy).

title: Two-Part Long Vowel Words
desc: decoding regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels
dir: Read each word out loud. Each word has two parts.
key: Mark each word read correctly. Each word has two syllables and at least one long vowel sound, such as pa-per, mu-sic, o-pen.
If the student breaks the word into syllables and then says it smoothly, count it correct.

title: Read the Lines
desc: decoding words with long vowels, vowel teams, prefixes, and suffixes in connected text
dir: Read each line out loud.
text: The tiger ate a tasty lunch. A baby robot made music.
key: Line 1: “The tiger ate a tasty lunch.” (every word read correctly)
Line 2: “A baby robot made music.” (every word read correctly)

title: Read the Fable
desc: an 82-word grade-level fable read aloud
dir: Read the story out loud. Use your best reading voice.
text: Crow played all summer. Mouse was busy dragging dry leaves into her hole. “Why are you working so hard?” asked Crow. “The rainy season is coming,” said Mouse. C
key: 82 words. Mark each missed word and each self-correction on the passage in the record sheet.
Note pace and expression in your notes.

title: Read It Again
desc: reading the same on-level text orally a second time with accuracy, rate, and expression
dir: Read the same text one more time. Make it smoother and more expressive.
text: Crow played all summer. Mouse was busy dragging dry leaves into her hole. “Why are you working so hard?” asked Crow. “The rainy season is coming,” said Mouse. C
key: Second reading of the same text. Count the words read correctly again and compare with the first reading. More words read correctly, fewer stops and rereads, and smoother phrasing show growth on succe
After the second reading ask: “What was the text about? Tell me two things you remember.” (an answer that matches the text on the screen)

title: Story Questions
desc: why and what questions about key details in a fable
dir: Answer each question out loud.
qs: Why was Mouse working so hard?
What happened to Crow when the rain came?
key: The rainy season was coming, so she was getting her home ready (dragging dry leaves into her hole). (RL.2.1)
Her nest got wet, she was cold and soaked, and she asked to stay with Mouse. (RL.2.1)

title: Retell and Lesson
desc: retelling a fable and telling its lesson
dir: Tell the story in your own words. Then answer out loud.
qs: Tell me what happened in the story, from beginning to end.
What lesson did Crow learn?
key: Retells in order: Crow played while Mouse worked, the rain came and soaked Crow’s nest, Mouse let her in, they fixed the nest together. (RL.2.2)
Get ready ahead of time. Don’t wait until the last minute. (RL.2.2)

title: Ask About the Story
desc: asking and answering who, what, where, when, why, and how questions about key details in a story
dir: Listen to the story. Then ask your teacher questions about it, and answer your teacher’s questions.
text: Listen to the story. Then ask me questions.
key: Read the story out loud once: Ben had a red kite. On Saturday he ran to the park. The wind was strong. The kite flew up high. Then the string snapped! Ben chased the kite down the hill. A girl named A
Say: “Ask me a who, what, or where question about the story.” (asks a real question that the story answers, for example who flew the kite, or where was the girl)

title: Listen Up
desc: describing key details from a text read aloud
dir: Listen first. Then answer your teacher’s questions out loud.
text: Listen carefully. Your teacher will read about sea otters.
key: What keeps otters warm? (thick fur)
Why do they wrap up in kelp? (so they don’t drift away)

title: Listen and Answer
desc: where, when, how, and what questions about an informational text the student read
dir: Listen while your teacher reads about sea turtles. Then answer each question out loud.
text: Sea Turtles Sea turtles live in warm oceans around the world. They come up to the top of the water. There they breathe air. A mother sea turtle crawls onto a be
qs: Where do sea turtles live?
When does the mother turtle crawl onto the beach?
key: In warm oceans around the world (RI.2.1)
At night (RI.2.1)

title: Find It and Write It
desc: gathering information from a text on the page to answer questions
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the Sea Turtles text again. Then find your answers. Say the first two out loud. Write the last one on your paper and hold it up.
qs: About how many eggs does a mother sea turtle lay? Find the part of the text that tells you.
About how long is it before the eggs hatch?
key: About one hundred. The student should point to the sentence about digging a hole and laying the eggs (W.2.8)
About two months (W.2.8)

title: Longer Directions
desc: following three- and four-step oral directions, requesting clarification when something is not understood, and giving multi-step directions
dir: Listen to your teacher. Do what you hear. Ask a question if you are not sure what to do. Then give a direction of your own.
text: Listen carefully. Do the steps in order. You need a pencil and paper.
key: Say once: “Stand up, push in your chair, and touch the door.” (does all three steps in order)
Say once: “Draw a square, color it blue, write your name inside it, and draw a dot above it.” (does all four steps in order)

title: Ask About the Facts
desc: asking and answering who, what, where, when, why, and how questions about key details in an informational text
dir: Listen to the facts. Then ask your teacher questions about them, and answer your teacher’s questions.
text: Listen to the facts. Then ask me questions.
key: Read the text out loud once: A bee is a small insect. Bees live in a hive. A hive is a home for many bees. Bees make honey from the sweet juice inside flowers. They fly from flower to flower to find f
Say: “Ask me a who, what, or where question about the facts.” (asks a real question that the text answers)

title: Remember and Write
desc: recalling information from experiences to answer a question in writing
dir: Think about what happened to you. Write one sentence on your paper for each question. Hold it up when you finish.
qs: Think about your morning. Tell about something you did and why you did it.
Think about a time you helped at home. What did you do?
key: Tells one real thing from their own morning and gives a reason. (a complete sentence)
Tells a real time and what they did. (a complete sentence)

title: Say It Right
desc: spoken grammar items (irregular plural, irregular past tense, reflexive pronoun, making a sentence longer)
dir: Say each answer out loud.
qs: One mouse, two ____.
Today I tell. Yesterday I ____.
key: mice (L.2.1)
told (L.2.1)

title: Write It Right
desc: written conventions (capital letters, an apostrophe in a contraction, a comma in a letter greeting, spelling a vowel team word)
dir: Write each answer on your paper and hold it up.
qs: Fix this sentence: the otters sleep near california
Write is not as one short word.
key: The otters sleep near California. (capital T, capital C, and a period) (L.2.2)
isn’t (with the apostrophe) (L.2.2)

title: Capital Letters
desc: capitalizing holidays, product names, and geographic names
dir: Listen while your teacher reads each sentence. Write it again with the right capital letters. Hold up your paper when you finish.
qs: Fix the capital letters: we eat turkey on thanksgiving.
Fix the capital letters: my family went to california in july.
key: We eat turkey on Thanksgiving.
My family went to California in July. (California; July may be accepted as a month name)

title: Use a Dictionary
desc: using a beginning dictionary and ABC order to check and correct spellings
dir: Listen. Answer out loud. If you have a beginning dictionary, you may use it.
qs: Put these words in ABC order the way a dictionary does: tiger, apple, mouse.
The guide words at the top of a dictionary page are cat and dog. Would the word cow be on this page? Tell why.
key: apple, mouse, tiger
Yes. cow comes after cat and before dog in ABC order.

title: Group Words
desc: using collective nouns
dir: Listen. Say the word that fits.
qs: Which word fits? A group of fish swimming together is called a ___. (school / pile)
Which word fits? A group of birds flying together is called a ___. (flock / bunch of rocks)
key: school. (A collective noun names a group.)
flock. (A collective noun names a group.)

title: Adjective or Adverb?
desc: using adjectives and adverbs and choosing between them depending on what is to be modified
dir: Listen. Pick the word that fits and say it.
qs: Which word tells how the dog runs: quick or quickly? “The dog runs ___.”
Which word describes the cat: soft or softly? “The ___ cat sat down.”
key: quickly (an adverb tells how)
soft (an adjective describes a noun)

title: Tell Me a Story
desc: telling about an experience in order, with details, in clear complete sentences
dir: Tell your story out loud. Say what happened first, next, and last.
text: Tell me about a time you helped someone. First Next Last
key: Tells events in order
Uses descriptive details

title: Plan and Tell a Story
desc: planning and delivering a short narrative presentation that recounts an event with details, a logical sequence, and a conclusion
dir: Pick one idea. Plan what you will say: the start, the middle, and the end. Then tell your story out loud.
text: Pick one: a day you will always remember, the time you tried something new, or a trip or a day away from home. Beginning Middle End
key: Plans first: says or draws what will happen at the start, the middle, and the end before telling (give about one minute to plan)
Tells one event with enough detail (who, where, and what happened)

title: Write About It
desc: an opinion letter about the fable
dir: Write on your paper. When you finish, hold it up. Or tell your teacher what you wrote.
text: Write a letter to Crow. Should she have gotten ready sooner? Tell her why, using the story. Write 3 or 4 sentences. Start with: Dear Crow End with: Your friend
key: States an opinion (W.2.1)
Gives a reason from the story (W.2.1)

title: Write About It
desc: an informative piece about sea turtles
dir: Write on your paper. When you finish, hold it up. Or tell your teacher what you wrote.
text: Write about sea turtles. Teach your reader 2 or more facts from Sea Turtles. Write 3 or 4 sentences. Look back at Sea Turtles Sea turtles live in warm oceans ar
key: Introduces the topic (W.2.2)
Gives 2 or more facts about sea turtles (W.2.2)

title: Write About It
desc: a narrative about a real experience
dir: Write on your paper. When you finish, hold it up. Or tell your teacher what you wrote.
text: Think of a time you got ready for something, like a trip, a game, or a rainy day. What did you do to get ready? Write a story about it. Write 3 or 4 sentences.
key: Tells about one event or a short set of events in order (W.2.3)
Includes details about actions, thoughts, or feelings (W.2.3)

title: What Is It Worth?
desc: telling the value of a digit in a three-digit number
dir: Look at the number. Answer out loud.
qs: What is the 4 worth?
What is the 7 worth?
key: 40, or 4 tens (2.NBT.A.1)
700, or 7 hundreds (2.NBT.A.1)

title: Write the Number
desc: writing a number in expanded form and writing a number from its name
dir: Write your answers on your paper and hold it up.
qs: Write 748 in expanded form.
Write “three hundred sixty” as a number.

title: Count It
desc: counting within 1000 and skip-counting by 100s
dir: Count out loud.
qs: Count out loud from 596 to 612.
Skip count by 100s from 230 to 930.

title: Count by 2s
desc: skip-counting by 2s within 1000
dir: Count out loud by 2s.
qs: Count by 2s from 10. Say the next six numbers.
Count by 2s from 58. Say the next five numbers.

title: Star Array
desc: finding the total of an array and writing it as a sum of equal addends
dir: Look at the stars. Write your adding sentence on your paper and hold it up.
qs: How many stars in all?
Write an adding sentence for them.
key: 12 stars (2.OA.C.4)

title: Odd or Even
desc: telling odd from even and writing an even number as a double
dir: Look at the dots. Answer out loud. Write the double on your paper.
qs: Is Group A odd or even? Write it as a double.
Is Group B odd or even?
key: Group A has 12: even, 6 + 6 (2.OA.C.3)
Group B has 15: odd (2.OA.C.3)

title: One Step
desc: one-step take-from, compare and put-together word problems within 100 with the unknown in different places
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the problem. Write your number sentence on your paper and hold it up.
qs: Mia had 52 stickers. She gave some away. Now she has 27. How many did she give away? Write a number sentence with a box for the number you don’t know.
Ben picked 34 apples. Rosa picked 18 more apples than Ben. How many did Rosa pick? Write a number sentence.
key: 34 + 18 = 52; answer 52 apples (2.OA.A.1)

title: Two Steps
desc: two-step addition and subtraction word problems within 100
dir: These problems have two steps. Listen while your teacher reads each one. Solve it on your paper and say your answer.
qs: Mia had 45 shells. She found 28 more. Then she gave 16 shells to a friend. How many shells does Mia have now?
There were 90 beads in the jar. Ben used 35 beads for one bracelet and 24 beads for another. How many beads are left?

title: Big Numbers
desc: adding and subtracting three-digit numbers with regrouping and showing a strategy
dir: Solve on your paper. Show your work and hold it up.
qs: Solve 356 + 248. Show how you did it.
Solve 500 - 237. Show how you did it.
key: 604, shows place value strategy or drawing (2.NBT.B.7)
263, regroups across the two zeros, or counts up from 237 (2.NBT.B.7)

title: Why Regroup?
desc: adding and subtracting within 1000 with place value, and explaining why a ten or hundred is composed or decomposed
dir: Solve on your paper. Show your work. Then tell why you had to regroup.
qs: Solve 53 + 29 with a drawing or a written method. Then tell why you had to make a new ten.
Solve 71 - 38. Tell why you had to take a ten apart.
key: 82. The ones made 12 (3 + 9), which is more than 9, so 10 ones were regrouped as 1 ten.
33. There were not enough ones (1 is less than 8), so 1 ten was broken into 10 ones.

title: Money
desc: counting coins, writing a dollar amount, and finding change, using the dollar sign and the cent sign
dir: Count the coins. Write the amount on your paper and hold it up.
qs: Maya has these coins in her pocket. How much money does she have? Write it with the right symbol.
Leo has 2 one-dollar bills and 3 quarters. Write how much money he has.
key: 63¢ (2.MD.C.8). $0.63 is also correct, but 63¢ is the grade 2 target.
$2.75 (2.MD.C.8). The dollar sign is part of the answer.

title: Time
desc: telling time to five minutes with a.m. or p.m. and knowing the minutes in an hour
dir: Look at the clock. Write the time on your paper. Then answer out loud.
qs: You eat breakfast at this time. Write the time. Is it a.m. or p.m.?
How many minutes are in an hour?
key: 60 minutes (2.MD.C.7)

title: Time Facts
desc: knowing relationships of time such as minutes in an hour, days in a month, and weeks in a year
dir: Listen. Answer out loud.
qs: How many minutes are in one hour?
About how many days are in one month?
key: 60 minutes
Between 28 and 31 days. 30 or 31 is the usual answer.

title: Fruit Graph
desc: finishing a bar graph with four categories and solving compare and put-together problems from it
dir: Tell your teacher how high to make the Oranges bar. Then answer the questions out loud.
text: 2 kids like oranges. Finish the graph.
qs: How many more kids like grapes than bananas?
How many kids like apples and oranges together?
key: Oranges bar filled to 2. Click the squares as the student tells you, or have them draw it on paper.
Grapes (7) minus bananas (3) = 4 more

title: Draw a Picture Graph
desc: drawing a picture graph from a data set with four categories and solving put-together, take-apart, and compare problems
dir: Look at the table. Draw a picture graph on your paper. Use one picture for each 1. Then answer out loud.
text: Favorite fruits: number of kids Choice Number of kids Apple 6 Banana 4 Grape 3 Pear 2
qs: Draw a picture graph of the table. Give it a title and label each row.
How many kids chose Apple and Banana together?
key: A picture graph with 6 symbols for Apple, 4 symbols for Banana, 3 symbols for Grape, 2 symbols for Pear. Each symbol stands for 1, the symbols are the same size and lined up, and the rows are labeled.

title: Draw a Bar Graph
desc: drawing a bar graph with a single-unit scale from a data set and solving put-together, take-apart, and compare problems
dir: Look at the table. Draw a bar graph on your paper. Count by ones up the side. Then answer out loud.
text: Ways to get to school: number of kids Choice Number of kids Walk 3 Bus 7 Car 5 Bike 2
qs: Draw a bar graph of the table. Give it a title, label each bar, and number the side by ones.
How many kids chose Car and Bike together?
key: A bar graph with bars of height 3 for Walk, 7 for Bus, 5 for Car, 2 for Bike, a title, labels, and a side scale counting by ones that starts at 0.

title: Measure It
desc: measuring an object with a ruler and choosing the right measuring tool
dir: Get a ruler and a spoon. Measure the spoon. Then answer out loud.
qs: Measure your spoon with a ruler. How long is it?
What tool would you use to measure a couch?
key: Lines up the ruler at 0 and gives a reasonable length with units (2.MD.A.1)
Yardstick or measuring tape (2.MD.A.1)

title: Shapes
desc: drawing and naming a five-sided shape and counting the faces of a cube
dir: Draw on your paper and hold it up. Then answer out loud.
qs: Draw a shape with 5 sides. What is it called?
How many faces does a cube have?
key: Pentagon (2.G.A.1)

title: Sun, Water and the Seed Patch
desc: reading the results of a plant test and planning a fair test of one thing a plant needs
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the chart. Then answer out loud.
text: The crew put three young palm shoots in sand on the deck and watched them for two weeks. Shoot What it got How it looked after two weeks 1 sunlight and water ta
qs: Which shoot grew best, and what did it get?
Shoot 2 had plenty of sunlight. Why did it do so badly?
key: Shoot 1. It got both sunlight and water.
It got no water. Sunlight on its own was not enough, so water is something a plant needs too.

title: Sun, Water and the Seed Patch
desc: making a simple model that does the job an animal does when it moves pollen or seeds
dir: Draw your model on your paper. Then tell your teacher about it.
text: On the island, bees carry pollen from flower to flower, and parrots carry seeds in their beaks to new ground. Draw a model you could really build out of things
qs: Draw your model. Label the part that picks the pollen up.
Which animal job does your model copy, and how does your model do that job?
key: Any model with a part that could carry pollen and a way to move it: a cotton ball or a fuzzy stick, a brush, a sticky paper cone. The labelled carrying part is what to look for.

The bee job, moving pollen from one flower to another. Accept a seed carrier instead if the drawing shows a scoop or a beak shape that holds a seed and drops it on new ground, which copies the parrot.

title: Two Places on the Island
desc: comparing the kinds of living things found in two different habitats
dir: Listen while your teacher reads both lists. Answer out loud.
text: The crew wrote down every living thing they saw in two places in one morning. The rock pool The palm grove 1 crab 1 parrot 1 snail 2 kinds of beetle 3 kinds of
qs: How many kinds of living things are on the rock pool list?
Name one living thing from one list that could not live in the other place, and say why.
key: 7. One crab, one snail, three seaweeds and two fish.

Any sensible pick with a reason: a small fish could not live in the palm grove because there is no water there to swim and breathe in; the palm tree could not live in the rock pool because its roots w

title: Fast, Slow and Where the Water Is
desc: using two sources as evidence that some Earth events happen quickly and some happen slowly
dir: Listen while your teacher reads both notes. Answer out loud.
text: Two notes about the island, from two different places. Where it came from What it says a page in the ship library book One storm wave can pull a whole shelf of
qs: Which note tells about a change to the land that happens quickly?
Which note tells about a change that takes a very long time?
key: The library book page, the shelf of sand pulled off in a single night.
The sign at the stone arch, cut over thousands of years.

title: Fast, Slow and Where the Water Is
desc: telling where water is found on Earth and whether it is solid or liquid
dir: Answer out loud.
text: Water turns up on nearly every part of the map the crew drew.
qs: Name three places on Earth where you would find water.
The ocean around the island is salty. Name a place where the water is fresh instead of salty.
key: Any three: the ocean, a river, a lake, a pond, a stream, rain in the clouds, snow or ice on a mountain, under the ground.
A river, a lake, a pond, a stream, or rain. Most of the water on Earth is in the ocean and is salty.

title: Holding the Land, and a Map of It
desc: comparing two things built to stop water from changing the shape of the land
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the chart. Answer out loud.
text: Waves kept washing the sand away from the path to the cove. The crew tried two ways to stop it and measured the sand that went missing each week. What was along
qs: Which one kept the most sand in place?
How do you know, using the chart?
key: the low wall of stones
Only 2 buckets of sand went missing with the wall, 5 went missing with the grass, and 14 went missing with nothing there. The reason has to come from the numbers.

title: Holding the Land, and a Map of It
desc: making a model of an area that shows the shapes of the land and the bodies of water in it
dir: Draw on your paper and hold it up.
text: Make your own model map of the island. Put in a hill, a flat stretch of land, a stream, and the ocean around it. Add a key that says which is which.
qs: Draw your model map with the hill, the flat land, the stream and the ocean on it.
Show me your key. Which parts are land and which parts are water?
key: All four on the page and told apart by shape or colour: a hill as a bump or as rings, flat land left flat, a stream as a line, the ocean around the outside.
Points to each part and reads the key. The key is the part that makes this a model and not just a picture.

title: Sorting the Supply Crate
desc: describing materials by properties you can see or feel and sorting them into groups
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the chart. Answer out loud.
text: The crew emptied a supply crate and wrote down what each thing was made of and what they noticed about it. Item Material What the crew noticed a cup metal hard,
qs: Sort the four items into a hard group and a group that is soft or bends easily.
You want a see through pile and a cannot see through pile. Which item goes in the see through pile?
key: Hard: the metal cup, the glass pane, the wooden lamp base. Soft or bends easily: the cloth sail patch. If a student leaves the wood out, ask them to look at its line again.
the glass window pane

title: Sorting the Supply Crate
desc: using test data to choose the material that suits a job
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the chart. Answer out loud.
text: The crew need a cover to keep rain off a stack of maps. They poured one cup of water over three materials and looked underneath, then pulled on each one. Materi
qs: Which material is best for the map cover?
Which two pieces of the chart make you sure?
key: the oiled canvas
No water got through it, and it does not tear when it is pulled. Both columns have to be used, not just one.

title: Pieces, Heat and Cold
desc: telling how a thing built from a few pieces can be taken apart and built into something new
dir: Answer out loud. You may draw if it helps.
text: A small crate is on deck. It is made of 6 flat boards. It has 12 nails. The crew pulled the nails out. They laid the boards in a row.
qs: The crate is gone. Are the boards gone too? What do the crew have now?
Build something new in your head out of those 6 boards. What is it, and how do the boards go together?
key: No. The boards are all still there. The crew have 6 boards and 12 nails, the same pieces, just not put together as a crate any more.

Any real thing from 6 flat boards: a bench, a shelf, a sign, a ramp, a small raft, a bird feeder. Listen for how the pieces join, because that is the evidence that the same set of pieces made somethin

title: Pieces, Heat and Cold
desc: arguing with evidence that some heating and cooling changes can be undone and some cannot
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the chart. Answer out loud.
text: Two things happened in the ship galley on the same morning. What happened A block of ice in a cup sat in the sun and turned into water. A hard biscuit sat on th
qs: Put the cup of water somewhere cold. What happens to it?
Put the black biscuit somewhere cold. Does it turn back into a hard biscuit?
key: It freezes back into ice. Cooling undoes the melting.
No. It stays black and crumbly. Nothing cold brings the biscuit back.

title: The Bucket That Slides
desc: naming a problem people want to fix and asking a question about it
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the note. Answer out loud.
text: Every time the ship rolls the bucket slides. The water bucket is by the galley door. It slides across the floor and spills. The crew mop it up and fill it again
qs: What is the problem the crew want to fix? Say it in one sentence.
Ask one question that would help you fix it.
key: The bucket slides across the floor and spills when the ship rolls. Naming the sliding, not the mopping, is the problem.
Any real question: how full is the bucket, how heavy is it, how smooth is the floor, how far does it slide, is there a corner it could sit in, could it be tied down. A statement is not a question, so

title: The Bucket That Slides
desc: drawing a design and telling how its shape does the job
dir: Draw on your paper and hold it up.
text: Draw something that would hold the bucket in one place. Think hard about its shape.
qs: Draw your fix.
Tell me how the shape of what you drew stops the bucket from sliding.
key: Any design that could really hold a bucket: a ring or hoop fixed to the floor, a crate the bucket sits down inside, a wooden rail across a corner, a short strap through a hook, a wide heavy base.
The shape is the part being checked. Something like: the ring goes all the way round so it cannot go sideways, the crate walls stop it, the strap is short so it can only move a little.

title: The Bucket That Slides
desc: comparing test results from two designs built for the same problem
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the chart. Answer out loud.
text: The crew built both fixes and sailed one whole day with each. Fix Times the bucket spilled that day a wooden ring nailed to the floor 0 a strap tied to a hook 3
qs: Which fix worked better?
How do you know?
key: the wooden ring nailed to the floor
The bucket spilled 0 times with the ring and 3 times with the strap. The reason has to come from the chart, not from liking rings.

title: Long Ago and Yesterday
desc: telling things that happened long ago from things that happened in the last day or two
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the four log lines. Answer out loud.
text: Four lines from the ship log. Line What it says 1 Sailors crossed this ocean in wooden ships with cloth sails, hundreds of years ago. 2 Yesterday the crew drew
qs: Which two lines tell about things that happened long ago?
Which two tell about things that happened in the last day or two?
key: Lines 1 and 3, the wooden sailing ships and finding the way by the stars.
Lines 2 and 4, the new map yesterday and the radio check this morning.

title: Where Things Are
desc: giving an exact place on a map with a letter and a number, and using north, south, east, west and between
dir: Look at the camp map. Answer out loud.
text: The crew camp, drawn in nine squares. North is at the top. 1 2 3 A palm grove tent seed patch B store fire ring map table C cove landing shell beach North is up
qs: Give the exact square the fire ring is in, using its letter and its number.
What is directly north of the fire ring?
key: B2
the tent, in square A2

title: Who Decides, and Who Trades
desc: telling who makes laws and leads here, and how other countries choose a leader differently
dir: Answer out loud.
text: Every place has people who make the rules and someone who leads.
qs: Who makes the laws for the whole country we live in? The people we vote for in Congress, or the crew of one ship?
What does a mayor do for a city?
key: the people we vote for in Congress
Leads the city and helps decide the rules there. Accept: runs the city, is in charge of the city, works with the city council.

title: Who Decides, and Who Trades
desc: telling what each side gives and gets in a trade, why people trade, and naming a job and what it produces
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the chart. Answer out loud.
text: The crew set up a small stall at the landing to swap what they have for what they need. Who What they bring What they want the net maker nets dried fish the fis
qs: The net maker and the fisher make a trade. What does each one give, and what does each one get?
Why do people trade instead of making everything themselves?
key: The net maker gives a net and gets dried fish. The fisher gives dried fish and gets a net.
Because nobody can make everything. Each person makes or does one thing well and trades for the rest. Accept: it saves time, you get what you cannot make yourself.

title: Someone Who Made a Difference
desc: telling what one person from the past did, naming a character strength, and saying how it helped others
dir: Listen while your teacher reads about her. Answer out loud.
text: Sally Ride loved science. She loved to find out how things worked. She trained hard. In 1983 she became the first. She was the first American woman to fly up. S
qs: What did Sally Ride do that no American woman had done before?
Which word fits her best from what you read: brave, careless, or unkind? Say why.
key: She flew into space. She was the first American woman to do it.
brave. Any reason taken from the text: she did a hard job nobody like her had done, she trained hard and went anyway when people said it was not for her.

title: Word Flip
desc: reading words with prefixes, suffixes, many syllables, and irregular spellings
dir: Read each word out loud. The last two are silly words. Just sound them out.
key: Read each word. mistrandful and replomable are silly words: listen for the prefix, the middle, and the suffix (mis-trand-ful, re-plom-a-ble).
Watch for: prefixes (pre-, dis-), suffixes (-less, -able, -ous), Latin suffix -tion (invention, celebration), multisyllable words (comfortable, remember), irregular words (thought, enough).

title: What Does the Ending Mean?
desc: identifying and knowing the meaning of common derivational suffixes and decoding words with Latin suffixes
dir: Read each word. Tell what the ending means and what the whole word means.
